questions.stem: Which two activities are part of security monitoring? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Security monitoring is the continuous collection and analysis of logs, events, and network activity to detect threats. It is ongoing and feeds detection and response.

questions.stem: A SIEM raised the alert below. What is the MAIN thing the SIEM added that the individual logs didn't?
questions.exhibit:
[SIEM] Correlated alert   severity=high
08:02  VPN      login jdoe from 203.0.113.80 (new country)
08:03  AD       jdoe added to group Finance-Share
08:05  FileSrv  jdoe read 1,240 files in 3 minutes

options.text: Linked three sources into one alert
options.rationale: Correct: correlation turns scattered events into meaning.

questions.explanation: A SIEM collects logs from many sources, correlates events, alerts, and retains data. Central collection plus correlation turns scattered events into meaningful alerts.
questions.discriminator_tested: Correlation turns scattered events into alerts.

questions.stem: Which factor would MOST push a company toward a cloud-hosted SIEM rather than one on its own servers?

options.text: A small team with no spare servers
A strict rule that logs stay onsite
Need for full control of the platform

questions.explanation: The SIEM hosting model is where the SIEM runs: on-premises or in the cloud. It is a deployment choice with trade-offs in control, cost, and maintenance.

questions.stem: What is the MAIN drawback of running a SIEM on-premises?

options.rationale: True, and part of the upkeep.

questions.explanation: An on-prem SIEM is hosted and maintained by the organization. It gives full control and keeps data local, but costs more upfront and needs maintenance and scaling effort.
questions.discriminator_tested: On-prem: higher upfront cost and maintenance.

questions.stem: A fast-growing startup with two security staff wants a SIEM that scales without buying servers. Which BEST fits?
questions.explanation: A cloud SIEM is a vendor-hosted service with elastic scaling and less maintenance. It depends on connectivity, and data location may be a concern.
questions.discriminator_tested: Cloud SIEM: elastic scaling, less maintenance.

questions.stem: Which two are detection methods a SIEM uses? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: SIEM detection methods are the techniques a SIEM uses to spot suspicious activity. Combine several; no single method catches everything.

questions.stem: A SIEM compares today's logins with each user's 30-day pattern, as shown below. What BEST describes the result?
questions.exhibit:
User     Usual logins (30-day baseline)   Today
jsmith   08:00-17:30, HQ                  08:12 HQ
akumar   09:00-18:00, HQ                  02:47 remote, new device
lchen    07:30-16:00, Branch              07:41 Branch

options.rationale: Correct: it deviates from the baseline.
True, but says nothing about normal.
A deviation needs investigation; it isn't proof.

questions.explanation: Baseline analysis establishes what normal activity looks like and compares current activity to it. The baseline is the reference; deviations are leads to investigate.
questions.discriminator_tested: Compare current activity to the baseline.

questions.stem: A team wants to catch attacks nobody has seen before and accepts more false positives as the price. Which method BEST fits?

options.rationale: Not a SIEM method, and slow.

questions.explanation: Anomaly detection flags activity that deviates from the baseline or expected pattern. It can catch unknown threats but raises more false positives than signature-based detection.

questions.stem: A detection model was trained on six months of logs from a period when an attacker was already inside the network. What is the MAIN risk?

options.text: It may learn the attack as normal
options.rationale: Correct: it depends on good data.
True, but not the specific risk.
Machine learning learns rather than using fixed rules.

questions.explanation: Machine learning algorithms learn patterns from data to detect threats. They learn from data rather than fixed rules, so they depend on good data and can still misclassify.
questions.discriminator_tested: Machine learning depends on good data.

questions.stem: A SOC lets its AI tool close any alert it rates low-risk, with no review. A real intrusion is closed this way. What BEST describes the flaw?

options.text: No human validation of AI results
options.rationale: Correct: AI augments analysts; it doesn't replace them.
Possibly, but review would have caught it anyway.

options.text: AI shouldn't be used in a SOC

questions.explanation: AI integration assists with triage, correlation, summarization, and prioritization. It augments analysts, and its results need human validation.

questions.stem: A behavior analytics tool raised the alert below. What MOST likely explains it?
questions.exhibit:
[UEBA] Risk score 92  entity=svc_backup
Usual:  logs on to BACKUP01 at 01:00 daily
Today:  logged on to 14 workstations between 13:20 and 13:31

options.rationale: Correct: the account is acting far outside its pattern.
True, but that restates the alert.

questions.explanation: UEBA (User and Entity Behavior Analytics) baselines users and devices and flags unusual behavior. It focuses on accounts and entities and helps find compromised accounts and insider threats.

questions.stem: A team wants its SIEM to flag connections to IP addresses already known to be used by attackers. Which data source BEST fits?

options.rationale: Correct: external lists of known bad IPs.

questions.explanation: Threat intelligence data is external feeds of known malicious IPs, domains, hashes, and attacker techniques. It is external context, versus an internal baseline.

questions.stem: An analyst compares a threat feed with a workstation scan, as shown below. What BEST describes the finding on WS-114?
questions.exhibit:
Threat feed: ransomware group indicators
  SHA-256  9f2c...e41a   (loader)
  Domain   update-cdn-check[.]com
  IP       198.51.100.23
WS-114 file scan:
  9f2c...e41a  C:\Users\Public\svc.exe

options.rationale: Correct: observable evidence the host may be compromised.
A weakness, not evidence of compromise.
Possibly, but it was matched against known-bad data.
A hash match is strong evidence.

questions.explanation: IoCs (Indicators of Compromise) are observable evidence that a system may be compromised: malicious IPs, file hashes, domains, unusual changes. They are often delivered through threat intelligence.
questions.discriminator_tested: IoC = evidence of compromise, often from threat intel.

questions.stem: What BEST distinguishes SOAR from a SIEM?

options.text: It acts on what was detected

questions.explanation: SOAR (Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response) coordinates tools and automates response workflows (playbooks). The SIEM detects and correlates; SOAR acts on what was detected.

questions.stem: A playbook enriches an alert with threat intel, opens a ticket, isolates the host through the EDR tool, and pages the on-call analyst. How is this BEST classified?

options.rationale: Correct: many steps across many tools.
There are four tasks and several tools.

questions.explanation: Orchestration vs automation: orchestration coordinates multiple tools and tasks into a workflow; automation performs a single task without human action.

questions.stem: Which two are typical consequences of failing to meet a data protection regulation? (Choose two.)
questions.explanation: Regulations and compliance are legal and industry requirements for protecting data; failure risks fines and legal action. They are external obligations, unlike internal policy.
questions.discriminator_tested: Failure risks fines and legal action.

questions.stem: A hospital is choosing a cloud backup provider with data centers in several countries. Which data locality question is MOST important?

options.rationale: Correct: locality is about physical location.

questions.explanation: Data locality is a requirement that data be stored or processed in specific geographic jurisdictions. It is about where data physically resides, and it affects cloud choices.

questions.stem: Which type of data does FERPA protect?
questions.explanation: FERPA (Family Educational Rights and Privacy Act) protects student education records in the US.

questions.stem: FISMA applies MOST directly to which organizations?
questions.explanation: FISMA (Federal Information Security Modernization Act) requires US federal agencies to run information security programs.

questions.stem: A credit union must protect its members' nonpublic personal information. Which law BEST applies?

options.rationale: Card data only, and a standard.

questions.explanation: GLBA (Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act) requires financial institutions to protect customers' nonpublic personal information.

questions.stem: A small online shop's owner says, "PCI DSS isn't a law, so we can skip it." What BEST describes the flaw in this reasoning?

options.text: Card brands enforce it by contract
options.rationale: Correct: merchants agree to it to accept cards.
It applies to anyone handling card data.
Card brands and acquirers enforce it.

questions.explanation: PCI DSS (Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard) protects cardholder data. It is an industry standard enforced through card-brand contracts, not a government law.

questions.stem: After a breach, a bank's compliance team formally informs its federal regulator about the incident. What is this activity?
questions.explanation: Reporting is the formal reporting of incidents and compliance status to regulators, management, or auditors: authorities and oversight.

questions.stem: State law requires notifying affected residents within 45 days of discovering a breach. Based on the timeline below, what BEST describes the problem?
questions.exhibit:
Mar 02  Breach detected (12,000 customer records)
Mar 04  Regulator informed
Mar 05  Containment complete
Jun 18  Customers informed by email

options.text: The regulator was told too early

questions.explanation: Notifications inform affected individuals or customers (and sometimes regulators) after a breach, within required timeframes. Deadlines vary by law.
